rows.notes: The study is a systematic literature review (SLR) of 214 articles on UAV imagery in agriculture (Section 3 Methodology; Table 6). It reports no own field data, experiment, survey or model runs; all findings (crop classification, disease detection, yield estimation, process monitoring, Section 4.5) are synthesised from cited primary studies. Q1 is therefore 'no' and Q2-Q9 follow. Even taken as a synthesis, the review documents detection of crop diseases and pests (Section 4.5.2) and some pesticide-spraying applications from other work, not its own evidence that UAVs mitigate pest or disease outbreaks; the claim of 'mitigating' outbreaks is downstream of the detection results the review summarises.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The document is a systematic literature review with no primary data; the 'meta-analysis' it mentions is a qualitative/quantitative synthesis of article counts, not an empirical result on any technology effect.
